sn36.7:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesalī in the Great Wood in the Hall with the Peaked Roof.
sn36.7:1.2: Then, in the evening, the Blessed One emerged from seclusion and went to the sick ward,
sn36.7:1.3: where he sat down in the appointed seat and addressed the bhikkhus thus:
sn36.7:2.1: “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should await his time mindful and clearly comprehending.
sn36.7:2.2: This is our instruction to you.
sn36.7:3.1: “And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu mindful?
sn36.7:3.2: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having put away covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn36.7:3.3: He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings …
sn36.7:3.5: phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having put away covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn36.7:3.6: It is in such a way that a bhikkhu is mindful.
sn36.7:4.1: “And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu exercise clear comprehension?
sn36.7:4.2: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is one who acts with clear comprehension when going forward and returning; when looking ahead and looking aside; when drawing in and extending the limbs; when wearing his robes and carrying his outer robe and bowl; when eating, drinking, chewing his food, and tasting; when defecating and urinating; when walking, standing, sitting, falling asleep, waking up, speaking, and keeping silent.
sn36.7:4.3: It is in such a way that a bhikkhu exercises clear comprehension.
sn36.7:4.4: “A bhikkhu should await his time mindful and clearly comprehending.
sn36.7:4.5: This is our instruction to you.
sn36.7:5.1: “Bhikkhus, while a bhikkhu dwells thus, mindful and clearly comprehending, diligent, ardent, and resolute, if there arises in him a pleasant feeling, he understands thus:
sn36.7:5.2: ‘There has arisen in me a pleasant feeling.
sn36.7:5.3: Now that is dependent, not independent.
sn36.7:5.6: But this body is impermanent, conditioned,
sn36.7:5.7: dependently arisen. So when the pleasant feeling has arisen in dependence on a body that is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, how could it be permanent?’
sn36.7:5.8: He dwells contemplating impermanence in the body and in pleasant feeling, he dwells contemplating vanishing, contemplating fading away, contemplating cessation, contemplating relinquishment.
sn36.7:5.9: As he dwells thus, the underlying tendency to lust in regard to the body and in regard to pleasant feeling is abandoned by him.
sn36.7:6.1: “Bhikkhus, while a bhikkhu dwells thus, mindful and clearly comprehending, diligent, ardent, and resolute, if there arises in him a painful feeling, he understands thus:
sn36.7:6.3: ‘There has arisen in me a painful feeling.
sn36.7:6.4: Now that is dependent, not independent.
sn36.7:6.7: But this body is impermanent, conditioned,
sn36.7:6.8: dependently arisen. So when the painful feeling has arisen in dependence on a body that is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, how could it be permanent?
sn36.7:6.9: ’ He dwells contemplating impermanence in the body and in painful feeling, he dwells contemplating vanishing, contemplating fading away, contemplating cessation, contemplating relinquishment.
sn36.7:6.10: As he dwells thus, the underlying tendency to aversion in regard to the body and in regard to painful feeling is abandoned by him.
sn36.7:7.1: “Bhikkhus, while a bhikkhu dwells thus, mindful and clearly comprehending, diligent, ardent, and resolute, if there arises in him a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he understands thus:
sn36.7:7.2: ‘There has arisen in me a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
sn36.7:7.3: Now that is dependent, not independent.
sn36.7:7.6: But this body is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen.
sn36.7:7.7: So when the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling has arisen in dependence on a body that is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, how could it be permanent?’
sn36.7:7.8: He dwells contemplating impermanence in the body and in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he dwells contemplating vanishing, contemplating fading away, contemplating cessation, contemplating relinquishment.
sn36.7:7.9: As he dwells thus, the underlying tendency to ignorance in regard to the body and in regard to neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is abandoned by him.
sn36.7:8.1: “If he feels a pleasant feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent’; he understands: ‘It is not held to’; he understands: ‘It is not delighted in.’
sn36.7:8.2: If he feels a painful feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent’; he understands: ‘It is not held to’; he understands: ‘It is not delighted in.’
sn36.7:8.3: If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent’; he understands: ‘It is not held to’; he understands: ‘It is not delighted in.’
sn36.7:8.4: “If he feels a pleasant feeling, he feels it detached;
sn36.7:8.5: if he feels a painful feeling, he feels it detached;
sn36.7:8.6: if he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he feels it detached.
sn36.7:8.7: “When he feels a feeling terminating with the body, he understands: ‘I feel a feeling terminating with the body.’ When he feels a feeling terminating with life, he understands: ‘I feel a feeling terminating with life.’
sn36.7:8.8: He understands: ‘With the breakup of the body, following the exhaustion of life, all that is felt, not being delighted in, will become cool right here.’
sn36.7:9.1: “Just as, bhikkhus, an oil lamp burns in dependence on the oil and the wick,
sn36.7:9.2: and with the exhaustion of the oil and the wick it is extinguished through lack of fuel,
sn36.7:9.3: so too, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu feels a feeling terminating with the body … terminating with life … He understands:
sn36.7:9.4: ‘With the breakup of the body, following the exhaustion of life, all that is felt, not being delighted in, will become cool right here.’”
